scenario_name: OpenAI Agents SDK-style Triage Handoff — Case 6 for AgentCoordKG
description: Hand-authored scenario following OpenAI Agents SDK's real Agent/Handoffs/Guardrails/Sessions schema (confirmed via official documentation), NOT a live SDK run. This is the fifth and final framework studied for AgentCoordKG, mirroring the five frameworks studied for HarnessKG. Provides a second independent confirmation that an explicit hand-off/delegation primitive (Handoffs, after CrewAI's allow_delegation) maps directly onto delegatesTask, and a fourth confirmation that a framework's persistent-memory primitive (Sessions) has no AgentCoordKG equivalent.

_openai_agents_sdk_native_log._comment: Mimics a real OpenAI Agents SDK run with a triage agent handing off to a billing specialist, using the SDK's actual primitives (Agent, handoff, input_guardrail, Session). Not itself part of the RDF instance data.

triage_agent.name: TriageAgent
triage_agent.instructions: Classify the request and hand off to the right specialist.

guardrail.name: billing_input_guardrail
guardrail.checks: is this actually a billing-related request?

session.description: Persistent memory layer maintaining working context across the handoff

run_trace.reason: request lacked a valid account identifier

_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Agent (instructions, tools): Maps directly to ak:Agent -- no ontology change needed.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Handoffs (control transferred to a speci: SECOND INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: maps directly to delegatesTask (Agent -> Task), joining CrewAI's allow_delegation as the second framework whose explicit hand-off/delegation primitive lands cleanly on this relation (distinct from the four dependsOn confirmations, which concern task ORDERING rather than delegation of RESPONSIBILITY).
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Input Guardrail tripwire (missing accoun: Interpreted (not native to the SDK in this exact form) as violatesConstraint -> Conflict -- the guardrail's compliance check is modeled as a Constraint that the initial handling Task violates, consistent with the governance-flavored Decision variant already noted in HarnessKG's OpenAI Agents SDK scenario, but here operationalized one step earlier as the Conflict-detection event itself.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Corrected re-run after guardrail failure: Maps to resolvesConflict (Task -> Conflict), consistent with the same resolution pattern used in all other AgentCoordKG framework scenarios.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Sessions (persistent memory layer): NO AgentCoordKG equivalent -- fourth independent confirmation (after CrewAI's Crew.memory=True, LangGraph's State/Checkpointer, MetaGPT's Memory) that a framework's persistent-memory primitive belongs entirely to HarnessKG (where Sessions would map directly to hk:Memory, as already confirmed in HarnessKG's own OpenAI Agents SDK scenario), never to AgentCoordKG.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Runner (executes the agent loop): NO AgentCoordKG equivalent -- AgentCoordKG has no orchestrating-container class analogous to HarnessKG's Harness; consistent with the same gap noted for CrewAI's Crew.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Final refund approval output: Interpreted (not native to the SDK) as triggering ak:Decision, consistent with the task-outcome Decisions found across all five AgentCoordKG framework scenarios.

instances.label: Corrected handling after account ID requested
Billing requests must include a valid account identifier
Input guardrail tripwire: missing account identifier
instances.rationale: The input guardrail flagged the request for lacking a valid account identifier, triggering tripwire_triggered=true.

instances.label: Decision to approve the $42.00 refund (interpreted, not native to the SDK)

story_summary: A Triage agent hands off a billing dispute to a Billing agent, but an automated guardrail flags the request for missing an account ID -- a conflict. After the account ID is obtained, the corrected request is processed and a refund is approved.
